input.content:
apiVersion: v3.2.0
kind: DataContract
id: example-shop-orders
name: orders
version: 1.0.0
status: draft
description:
  purpose: One row per order line. An order has several lines.
servers:
  - server: dev
    type: bigquery
    environment: dev
    project: example-project-dev
    dataset: example_shop
    location: europe-west2
schema:
  - name: orders
    physicalName: orders
    physicalType: table
    description: One row per order line. An order has several lines.
    properties:
      - name: order_id
        logicalType: string
        physicalType: STRING
        required: true
        primaryKey: true
        primaryKeyPosition: 1
        description: Identifier of the order. Repeats across the lines of one order.
      - name: line_no
        logicalType: integer
        physicalType: INT64
        required: true
        primaryKey: true
        primaryKeyPosition: 2
        description: Line number within the order. Together with order_id it identifies a row.
      - name: sku
        logicalType: string
        physicalType: STRING
        description: Stock keeping unit of the ordered product.
      - name: quantity
        logicalType: integer
        physicalType: INT64
        description: Quantity ordered on this line.
      - name: unit_price
        logicalType: number
        physicalType: NUMERIC
        description: Price per unit on this line.
      - name: ordered_at
        logicalType: timestamp
        physicalType: TIMESTAMP
        description: Time the order was placed.

I saved the contract to `contracts/orders.yaml`. I haven't validated it against the ODCS JSON schema.

- **Server:** I added a `dev` BigQuery server using the project, dataset and location from `AGENTS.md` and the table doc: `example-project-dev`, `example_shop` and `europe-west2`.

- **Metadata:** I set the status to `draft` and the version to `1.0.0`. The id `example-shop-orders` is a placeholder I made up.
- **Descriptions:** I wrote the column descriptions myself, since the doc only gives names and types. Please check them.

I left out nullability, quality rules, SLAs and ownership because the sources don't specify them.
